source.title: Feature-Level Insights into Artificial Text Detection with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: K. Kuznetsov; Laida Kushnareva; P. Druzhinina; Anton Razzhigaev; Anastasia Voznyuk; Irina Piontkovskaya; Evgeny Burnaev; Serguei Barannikov

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether SAE-derived features in an LLM provide useful, recoverable feature-level information, using text-detection and feature-level analyses rather than the original toy-model geometry experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper measures classification performance using SAE features and describes individual features' detection performance. It also reports steering effects, but those are deliberately induced changes in generation and do not establish that the behaviors arise naturally. Detailed numerical classifier values are presented in figures and are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: This is an applied artificial-text-detection study. It uses pre-trained Gemma Scope SAEs as a tool and reports only its own pipeline's results: detection F1 for SAE-feature classifiers versus mean-pooled activations, single-feature threshold classifiers, and feature interpretation and steering. None of its results measure whether features are superposed, whether they spread across neurons, or whether the SAE recovers the model's features. Detection accuracy of a downstream classifier does not bear on V4. The line 'removing superposition helps the classifier' is the authors' interpretation, not a measurement. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SAE-based analysis is a valuable tool for understanding text generators, detectors and detector generalization. They also report that detection is easy with default prompts but hard when prompt style changes. Additional claims: SAE features outperform raw activations for detection, and modern LLMs show a distinct style, especially in information-dense domains.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pre-trained Gemma-Scope SAEs on Gemma-2-2B residual streams, then evaluates feature-based text detection and interprets or steers selected features. It does not reproduce the original toy-network feature-generation or geometric-superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports variation in detection across generating-model families and domains; detection is weaker for older flan and t0 models, and the authors say personalized prompt styles make detection more difficult.

fits_no_version.finding: On COLING, XGBoost on summed SAE features beats XGBoost on mean-pooled residual activations across Train, Dev, Devtest and Test (figure only). At layer 16 it also beats the state-of-the-art MTL detector. The authors attribute this to 'removing superposition'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature bases improve downstream linear and tree classifier performance over raw activations (a utility claim, not a superposition claim).

fits_no_version.finding: The study's interpretations of features 3608 and 4645 (manual reading plus steering) are broader than Neuronpedia's narrow auto-labels. This suggests single-label feature descriptions can be misleading.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auto-interp labels of SAE features are incomplete relative to multi-method interpretation.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The analysis uses a single SAE on the residual stream of Gemma-2-2B. Numerical classifier results are mainly in figures, with no uncertainty estimates stated in the text. The authors also note that some SAE features are difficult to interpret and that the examined attacks are only a subset of possible attacks.
record.rows_left_out: Steering outcomes in Table 7 and Appendix G were omitted because the paper deliberately induces changes by shifting feature activations; those outcomes do not establish naturally occurring model behavior or directly test the recoverability claim. Detailed figure-only domain/model results beyond the explicitly described findings were not extracted as separate rows.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Does not measure feature spread across neurons or the quality of SAE recovery (reconstruction, sparsity, interpretability rates). It only uses the SAE features downstream.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity, beyond an anecdotal disagreement with Neuronpedia labels.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'tests' and its labels are dropped. Using SAE features successfully for a downstream task is tool use (T4), not a test of whether models contain recoverable sparse features. There are no numerical values in the text; all results are figure-only. Steering results are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks, feature overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometric arrangements.
Does not test whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

Tests SAE-derived features in one residual-stream SAE setup on Gemma-2-2B, but does not measure feature spread across neurons or establish that the SAE recovers all relevant model features; results do not establish generality across LLMs or SAEs.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
Uses SAE decoder directions for individual features but does not test whether model features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Trained XGBoost classifiers on SAE-derived features and compared them with classifiers on mean-pooled layer activations.

conditions.value: remaining data, including Dev, Devtest, and Test subsets
16th layer; the paper also evaluates multiple layers

rows.value: Figure only; the text states that SAE features outperform activations in training and across other subsets, with both methods degrading slightly on other subsets.
rows.note: The paper attributes the advantage to removing superposition, but does not state numerical F1 values in the text.
rows.check: This row compares the study's own method (XGBoost on SAE features) with an alternative (XGBoost on mean-pooled activations) on detection F1. That is method performance, not a measure of superposition or of feature recoverability. 'observed' against V4 is unjustified. Values are figure-only (Fig. 2).

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated SAE features 3608 and 4645 using threshold classifiers for artificial-text detection.

conditions.value: older models, including flan and t0

rows.value: Figure only; the text states that universal-feature performance drops below random for older models such as flan and t0.
rows.note: The text describes the universal features collectively; it does not give separate numerical values for features 3608 and 4645.
rows.check: Single-feature detection F1 on older generators (flan, t0) says nothing about whether SAEs recover model features. 'reversed' against V4 is a category error: below-random detection is a property of the ATD task, not the opposite of V4.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated SAE feature 8264 using a threshold classifier for artificial-text detection.
rows.value: Figure only; the text describes performance as near-perfect.
rows.note: The paper says feature 8264 has near-perfect performance for GPT3.5+; no numerical value is stated in the text.
rows.check: Near-perfect detection by feature 8264 on GPT3.5+ is task performance, not evidence bearing on V4. The value is figure-only and qualitative.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated SAE-derived features 3608, 4645, 6587, 8264, and 14161 using threshold classifiers.
rows.value: The text states that these features perform well on the listed modern LLM families, especially in the listed domains; figure values are not stated.
rows.note: The reported outcome is a collective description for the listed features, models, and domains.
rows.check: This is a collective qualitative description of the detection performance of selected features. It does not measure superposition or feature recovery.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
